newsitem.title: PERU: Peru, rebels seek to negotiate peaceful solution.
newsitem.headline: Peru, rebels seek to negotiate peaceful solution.

text.p: Government negotiators and Marxist guerrillas held a fresh round of talks on Monday seeking a bloodless solution to the crisis that has kept 72 weary diplomats, officials and businessmen captive for 69 days.

A Red Cross car drove a Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) representative -- believed to be its leader Nestor Cerpa -- from the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence to a nearby safe house used for negotiations.

Rebels inside the residence broadcast their revolutionary anthem commemorating dead comrades and shouted defiant slogans as Cerpa, apparently accompanied by his No. 2 Rolly Rojas, was driven to the talks.
"We are the ones who have taken the Japanese residence. Until death, damn it!" they shouted.

The MRTA representatives met with government negotiator Domingo Palermo, who was waiting with two advisers, three members of a guarantors commission overseeing the talks and the Japanese government's observer Terusuke Terada.

A metal detector was used to ensure nobody took arms into the two-floor building flying Red Cross flags. It was the fifth meeting since talks began on Feb. 11 after weeks of intransigence over the guerrillas' central demand for the release of some 400 jailed comrades.
Although both sides have agreed not to divulge details of the talks, guarantors overseeing the negotiations indicated after the fourth round last week that progress was being made.

President Alberto Fujimori said over the weekend that Cerpa's presence for the first time at Thursday's meeting was "a small advance" towards a peaceful solution. But he said the rebel chief spent a lot of his time attacking the government.
The hostages include Fujimori's brother, two government ministers, high-ranking security and judiciary officials and the envoys of Japan and Bolivia.

A statement from the guarantors said the last session had broached "important issues", but gave no more details. Japan's Mainichi Shimbun newspaper said on Monday that Fujimori had agreed to include the rebels' demand for release of their comrades on the agenda of the negotiations.

Palermo and Cerpa also discussed improving jail conditions for MRTA prisoners at Thursday's meeting, the paper said, quoting an unnamed source close to the talks. Another possible government concession discussed was allowing prisoners more family visits, the source said.

A government spokesman told Reuters he could not comment on the newspaper report. The rebel demand for the release of prisoners has been the main stumbling block in the talks, but congressmen hinted last week that a deal might be in sight.

Those imprisoned include 27-year-old American Lori Berenson, who is serving a life sentence in a grim jail high up in the Andes after being convicted by a military court of helping plot a foiled MRTA assault on Peru's Congress.
